text: gemma.ai is Google DeepMind's Gemma documentation site: its pages are titled '… - Gemma Documentation' and carry the footer 'Copyright © 2026 Google DeepMind'; the ai.google.dev/gemma/docs pages the reference cites (prompt-formatting-gemma4, mtp/mtp) still resolve on 2026-10-15, and gemma.ai's Gemma 4 prompt-formatting text matches ai.google.dev's apart from layout, a reworded opening sentence, gemma.ai's added Gemma 1-3 and 'What's next' sections, and one token spelling: gemma.ai's function-calling table writes the tool-definition token as '<|tool|>' where ai.google.dev, and both sites' examples, have '<|tool>'.

verifier_note: Fetched 2026-10-15. Titles on 8 gemma.ai pages: 'Prompt Formatting - Gemma Documentation', 'Releases - Gemma Documentation', 'LiteRT-LM - Gemma Documentation', 'Speed-up Gemma 4 with Multi-Token Prediction - Gemma Documentation', 'A Visual Guide to MTP - Gemma Documentation', 'Tool calling - Gemma Documentation', 'A Visual Guide to Gemma 4 - Gemma Documentation', 'Quantization-Aware Training - Gemma Documentation'. Each has the footer 'Copyright © 2026 Google DeepMind', followed by 'Made with Zensical' and a cookie banner, so 'end with' is loose. Both ai.google.dev URLs return HTTP 200 with no redirect: 'Gemma 4 Prompt Formatting | Google AI for Developers' (Last updated 2026-06-03 UTC) and 'Gemma 4 Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) using Hugging Face Transformers | Google AI for Developers'. Both quotes found verbatim. Word diff of gemma.ai from 'Prompt formatting' to 'Gemma 1-3' (1,348 words) against ai.google.dev's body (1,336 words), similarity ratio 0.981. Differences: (1) the opening, gemma.ai 'Gemma 4 introduced a new set of control tokens. Gemma 1 through 3 use an older <start_of_turn> format, kept below because those models are still in use.' against 'Starting with Gemma 4, we introduce new control tokens. For Gemma 3 and lower, see the previous document.'; (2) the 'Defines a tool' row of the token table, gemma.ai '<|tool|> <tool|>' (raw HTML <|tool|>) against ai.google.dev '<|tool> <tool|>'; gemma.ai's own example uses '<|tool>'; (3) 'Note' against 'Note:' twice (admonition layout); (4) 'the word thought' (code style) against 'the word "thought"'; (5) gemma.ai 'Execution \& Injection' (a stray backslash) against 'Execution & Injection'. gemma.ai also adds an h2 'Gemma 1-3' (with an h3 'System instructions') and an h2 'What's next'.

text: Google's gemma.ai LiteRT-LM page says LiteRT-LM's MTP speeds up decoding 'with no quality loss: up to 2.2x on mobile GPUs and 1.5x on mobile CPUs', without naming devices, files or dates, and recommends MTP for every task on GPU backends and for E4B on CPU, and selectively for E2B on CPU, where it can slow freeform generation slightly.

sources.quote: LiteRT-LM supports MTP, which speeds up decoding with no quality loss: up to 2.2x on mobile GPUs and 1.5x on mobile CPUs.
Google recommends MTP for every task on GPU backends, and for E4B on CPU.

verifier_note: https://gemma.ai/deployment/litert/ fetched 2026-10-15. Both quotes found verbatim. The rest of the MTP section reads: 'On E2B on CPU it helps most with rewriting, summarizing and coding, but can slow down freeform generation slightly — so enable it selectively there.' The section names no device, file or date. The page's only device reference is in 'Model sizes' ('Google publishes measured prefill, decode and time-to-first-token figures per device and backend on the Gemma 4 LiteRT-LM page'), which is a link and not about MTP.

text: gemma.ai's LiteRT-LM page gives .litertlm bundle sizes of 2.58 GB (E2B) and 3.65 GB (E4B) without naming a source; they match the litert-community cards' 'Model size' figures (2,583 and 3,654 MB) in GB, while the pinned plain files are 2,588,147,712 and 3,659,530,240 bytes (2.588 and 3.660 GB), so the page's figures are a little below the files' sizes. The page says LiteRT-LM ships E2B and E4B 'with larger models coming'.

sources.quote: LiteRT-LM ships E2B and E4B, with larger models coming.

formula: 2,588,147,712 B = 2.588 GB; 3,659,530,240 B = 3.660 GB (decimal); the page's 2.58 and 3.65 match the cards' 2,583 and 3,654 MB (MOD-FAM-046)
verifier_note: Page 'Model sizes' table: 'Size | .litertlm bundle | E2B 2.58 GB | E4B 3.65 GB', with no source given. Quote 'LiteRT-LM ships E2B and E4B, with larger models coming.' found verbatim. generated/models/e2b-google.md line 6: 'gemma-4-E2B-it.litertlm, 2,588,147,712 bytes'. e4b-google.md line 6: 'gemma-4-E4B-it.litertlm, 3,659,530,240 bytes'. Recomputed 2.588147712 and 3.65953024 GB (2.410 and 3.408 GiB). MOD-FAM-046 records 'Model size' as 2583 and 3654 MB. Re-fetched the cards at b3ca0d2f and 2eee7ac3: rows '| iPhone 17 Pro | GPU | 2,878 | 56.5 | 0.3 | 2583 | 1450 |' and '| iPhone 17 Pro | GPU | 1,189 | 25.1 | 0.9 | 3654 | 3380 |', and the cards say 'Model size is the size of the file on disk.' 2,583 MB is 2.58 GB and 3,654 MB is 3.65 GB, so the figures match. But the page cites no source, and truncating the files' own sizes also gives 2.58 and 3.65 (rounding gives 2.59 and 3.66). 'Which are the cards' figures' asserts a provenance the page doesn't state; 'match' is what the sources support. The arithmetic in 'formula' is correct.

text: gemma.ai's LiteRT-LM page documents exporting a Hugging Face Gemma 4 checkpoint (fine-tuned or not) to .litertlm with the litert-torch-nightly package: 'litert-torch export_hf --model=google/gemma-4-E2B-it' with --externalize_embedder and --jinja_chat_template_override=litert-community/gemma-4-E2B-it-litert-lm; the page doesn't explain that flag beyond its name and value.

sources.quote: Export Safetensors — including a model you have fine-tuned — to the .litertlm format: uv tool install litert-torch-nightly litert-torch export_hf

verifier_note: Quotes found verbatim. The full block reads 'uv tool install litert-torch-nightly / litert-torch export_hf \ --model=google/gemma-4-E2B-it \ --output_dir=/tmp/gemma4 \ --externalize_embedder \ --jinja_chat_template_override=litert-community/gemma-4-E2B-it-litert-lm', then 'litert-lm run /tmp/gemma4/model.litertlm ...'. The original's 'which takes the chat template from the litert-community repository' is a reading of the flag's name; the page never says what the flag does. Also: the block has class 'model-swap', so the site's model selector (javascripts/model-switcher.js with model-data.js) can rewrite both IDs to the E4B ones (hf 'google/gemma-4-E4B-it', litert 'litert-community/gemma-4-E4B-it-litert-lm'). E2B is the served default.
original_text: gemma.ai's LiteRT-LM page documents exporting a Hugging Face Gemma 4 checkpoint (fine-tuned or not) to .litertlm with the litert-torch-nightly package: 'litert-torch export_hf --model=google/gemma-4-E2B-it' with --externalize_embedder and --jinja_chat_template_override=litert-community/gemma-4-E2B-it-litert-lm, which takes the chat template from the litert-community repository.

text: gemma.ai's MTP page says Gemma 4's drafter (the 'lightweight 4-layer MTP drafter') gives speedups 'while guaranteeing the exact same quality as standard autoregressive generation', and shows it only with Hugging Face Transformers and do_sample=False; gemma.ai's MTP visual guide, reposted from Exploring Language Models, says 'similar quality' instead.

sources.quote: This results in significant decoding speedups while guaranteeing the exact same quality as standard autoregressive generation
These enhancements result in significant decoding speedups while guaranteeing similar quality

verifier_note: https://gemma.ai/get-started/capabilities/mtp/ fetched 2026-10-15. Quote found: '...decoding speedups while guaranteeing the exact same quality as standard autoregressive generation, making these checkpoints perfect for low-latency and on-device applications.' Also found: 'Drafter (e.g., google/gemma-4-E2B-it-assistant): The lightweight 4-layer MTP drafter that proposes candidate tokens'. The only code is Transformers (h2 'Run MTP with Transformers', Uses: Transformers, Colab), and both target_model.generate calls pass do_sample=False. Visual guide https://gemma.ai/tutorials/visual-guides/mtp/: 'Originally published as part of A Visual Guide to Gemma 4 on Exploring Language Models.' and '...decoding speedups while guaranteeing similar quality, making these checkpoints perfect...'. The MTP page also says the 26B A4B drafter may not speed up at batch size 1, which doesn't contradict the claim.

text: gemma.ai's function-calling page runs google/gemma-4-E2B-it with Hugging Face Transformers and its Hugging Face chat template (processor.apply_chat_template) and shows the model's tool-call output ending '<tool_call|><|tool_response>'; it gives no token IDs, shows no E4B output, and says nothing about LiteRT-LM or the .litertlm file's template.
verifier_note: https://gemma.ai/get-started/capabilities/function-calling/ (title 'Tool calling - Gemma Documentation'). Found 'MODEL_ID = "google/gemma-4-E2B-it"', AutoModelForMultimodalLM, processor.apply_chat_template(..., tools=...), and the exact output 'Output: <|tool_call>call:get_current_weather{location:<|"|>Tokyo, JP<|"|>}<tool_call|><|tool_response>'. The page has no token IDs (no '50' anywhere), so 'that is with stop token 50' isn't supported by the cited source. If it stays, cite generated/hf/google__gemma-4-E2B-it/generation_config.json (eos_token_id [1, 106, 50]) plus the tokenizer ID of <|tool_response>. 'E4B' and 'litertlm' appear nowhere in the HTML; 'LiteRT-LM' appears only in the site navigation. The MODEL_ID block is a 'model-swap' block, so the site's model selector can rewrite the ID to another size; the printed outputs are static.

text: gemma.ai's 'A Visual Guide to Gemma 4' (reposted from Exploring Language Models) lists K=V among changes that relate to all model sizes and says local layers have 2 query heads per KV head and global layers 8; the pinned E2B and E4B configs set attention_k_eq_v false, num_global_key_value_heads null and 8 query heads on 1 (E2B) or 2 (E4B) KV heads, so K=V and the 2:1 local grouping hold for neither model, E4B's 4:1 grouping matches neither figure, and only E2B's 8:1 matches the guide's global-layer figure.

sources.quote: The local attention layers use GQA and have 2 Query heads sharing one KV head.
There are a number of things that were changed compared to Gemma 3 that relate to all model sizes:

sources.detail: text_config rows attention_k_eq_v, num_attention_heads, num_key_value_heads, num_global_key_value_heads for gemma-4-E2B-it and gemma-4-E4B-it

conflicts_with: gemma.ai visual guide: K=V for all sizes; 2:1 local and 8:1 global query-to-KV grouping
verifier_note: The guide's shared-architecture section: 'There are a number of things that were changed compared to Gemma 3 that relate to all model sizes: Interleaving Layers – ...; K=V – The Keys are set to be equivalent to the Values only for the global attention; p-RoPE – ...'. Its GQA subsection (shared section, before the per-model sections): 'The local attention layers use GQA and have 2 Query heads sharing one KV head. With Gemma 4, the global attention layers are made more efficient by having 8 Query heads to share one KV head.' The E2B & E4B section says nothing else about heads. Attribution: 'Originally published on Exploring Language Models.' hf-configs.md rows (E2B | E4B): text_config.attention_k_eq_v False | False; num_attention_heads 8 | 8; num_key_value_heads 1 | 2; num_global_key_value_heads None | None. In config.json the key is present with value null. Error in the original: E2B has 8 query heads per KV head in every layer, so its global layers do match the guide's 8. 'Neither holds for E2B' is wrong for that half, and 'no num_global_key_value_heads' should read null.
original_text: gemma.ai's 'A Visual Guide to Gemma 4' (reposted from Exploring Language Models) lists K=V among changes that relate to all model sizes and says local layers have 2 query heads per KV head and global layers 8; neither holds for E2B or E4B, whose pinned configs set attention_k_eq_v false, 8 query heads on 1 (E2B) or 2 (E4B) KV heads in every layer, and no num_global_key_value_heads.
